current_history.author: holeen
current_history.message:
fix(gateway): harden Responses recovery and Anthropic stream errors

Responses requests could lose current-turn history or usage after upstream
errors, and completed or cancelled recovery could remain an Ops failure.
Unify recovery evidence, context ownership and turn lifecycle across HTTP,
native WebSocket, HTTP bridge and passthrough without changing client models.

Preserve encrypted reasoning and compaction. Remove legacy ciphertext deletion,
blind predecessor deletion and cross-mode stripping. Repair explicit persisted
item rejections only from self-contained input, retaining call_id pairing and
complete encrypted content. Collect late same-ID ciphertext without mutating
earlier snapshots. An unresolved context rejection requires complete client
history, never another account or an incomplete reasoning item.

Separate complete same-owner replay from cross-account portability. Capacity
errors may retry the owner with full encrypted history; private files, vector
stores, containers and unresolved persisted state cannot move between accounts.
Evaluate namespace children and dynamic additional_tools/tool_search_output
inventories. Allow client discovery and read-only search; refuse execution tools,
unknown or ambiguous definitions and opaque tool context. Repeated read-only
search may incur upstream usage. Do not replay after committed output.

Stage metadata and response identity within 8 MiB and one second from identity.
Recover safe EOF/1012 and connection-limit failures without exposing discarded
response IDs. Rotate native leases at 55 minutes, retaining valid persisted
anchors for store=true. Bare errors remain provisional until authoritative
output, terminal or configured idle expiry; definitive pre-response parameter
rejections finish promptly. Preserve upstream error evidence and map capacity
errors to 503 while delivering the existing client-compatible error code.

Use one client reader, serialized writes and bounded queues. Keep cancellation
on the active turn and credential. A rejected create with no response identity
returns a request error; completed rejection does not require closing the client
socket. Failed attempts do not become replay history. Bridge warmup remains a
bounded local control turn without inference or billing. Bridge strips the WS
envelope from HTTP and restores lane/error correlation on WS events. This still
admits one lane per socket, not multiplexing.

Revalidate later-turn keys, ungrouped keys, account authorization, group/model
eligibility and effective upstream configuration. Rebuild the upstream after
credential, proxy, endpoint or mode changes only with sufficient ownership and
context evidence. Freeze account/user/model/request billing snapshots. Retain
observed partial usage after bounded cancellation/drain; never estimate missing
usage or bill discarded attempts. Invalid encrypted input is not an account
health failure.

Use existing opt-in attempt and first-output budgets across admission, scheduling,
backoff and upstream operations. Cover headers and body for native HTTP,
passthrough and bridge, and stop the first-output timer after semantic content.
Zero retains per-path defaults. Pre-send exhaustion and client cancellation do
not penalize an account that received no request. Refresh replay policy from
the final transformed request, including injected image tools.

Persist bounded retry-stop diagnostics: actual mode/protocol, created-to-failure
delay, semantic/metadata commitment, tool blocker, context scope and remaining
budget. Keep prompt/output/ciphertext out of these diagnostics. Confirm recovered
Ops outcomes per turn and preserve observed upstream status alongside client
request status. Explicit logging levels avoid error-keyword promotion.

Trace HTTP connection/send boundaries and propagate proven-unsent evidence,
including plugins. Retry transient proxy TLS handshakes only before send with
a rewindable body, adapting that narrow mechanism from
ranxi2001/sub2api@11be589504b482d77827ab383b4b53f777241238.
Feed H2 body/protocol failures into the bounded expiring fallback map without
treating provider capacity errors as proxy protocol failures.

Keep the existing scheduler, transactional usage, Grok-specific conversions,
brand channels, security boundaries and manual release workflow. Production
transport canaries and multi-lane/steering remain separate gated work.

Correct Anthropic overloaded_error classification after message_start or SSE
keepalives (#14165): preserve semantic 529 and the overload client response,
while retaining pre-output cooldown policy and the no-replay guard.
Regression checks cover both post-output cases, Ops diagnostics and
pre-output versus committed-stream client responses.

Treat codex.rate_limits and codex.response.metadata as lifecycle metadata
for first-output deadlines and recovery progress. Preserve numeric WS
event counts through Ops redaction without exposing credentials or
non-numeric values. Keep the existing post-commit replay boundary.

current_history.message:
feat(bps): integrate Excel routing and reliable Responses WebSocket bridge

Port the BPS protocol core and selected account, credential, tool, image,
and admin controls onto the native gateway. Keep BPS disabled by default.
Share the BPS HTTP/SSE path with client WebSocket turns and Messages/Chat
compatibility through the existing gateway and apicompat conversion.

Preserve native history, response ownership, cancellation, attempt budgets,
partial usage, error contracts and terminal-event precedence. Route and
refresh accounts by the selected model independently of native WS mode;
isolate bridge sessions and retain usage through repair and compaction
failure, EOF, cancellation and failover. Reject opaque server context,
keep billing IDs out of response lineage, and preserve Excel-only guards,
native compact mapping and local Fast policy.

Restore native account switching for explicit BPS model rejection and safe
pre-output transient failures across HTTP/SSE, WS and compatibility routes.
Preserve absolute turn deadlines, cancellation and no-replay guards, actual
usage, per-model cooldowns and filtered discovery. Freeze redacted upstream
diagnostics before Ops snapshots, attribute repair failures to their actual
request IDs, and retain logical failure status after SSE keepalives.

Resolve declared tool names consistently across direct and wrapped BPS
calls, retaining exact namespace priority and bounded redacted catalog
diagnostics. Classify explicit BPS overload identifiers as 503 so existing
safe failover handles them without widening replay or attempt budgets.

The latest catalog and overload changes passed focused unit tests, complete
protocol and expanded BPS/WS race suites, boundary regressions repeated 20
times, and server builds. Source manifests and manual-only release workflow
checks passed; detailed validation history remains in the dual-path audit.

Preserve complete BPS terminal JSON tails across late body read errors and
continue downstream failure event sequences. Distinguish clean EOF without
a terminal from transport errors; freeze safe stream diagnostics with the
actual upstream HTTP identity without replaying accepted generations.

Use a scoped source port to exclude retired and unrelated operations.
Record requirements, the dual-path audits, per-file source provenance and
a read-only review tool for subsequent upstream updates.

Previously completed validation: full backend unit suite; BPS/Excel/WS and
basispoints/transportdiag race suites; focused failure tests repeated 20
times; server build, Wire check and integration-test compilation; frontend
build and 29 focused tests; manual-release workflow tests. The final full
backend suite passed on rerun after one unrelated runtime snapshot timeout;
20 isolated repeats each on current and baseline passed. Real BPS requests
and PostgreSQL/Redis runtime integration were not executed.

Squash the implementation and final reliability review into one portable
commit. Preserve the final reviewed file tree exactly; retain historical
audit references in the documentation and original commits in local backups.
